label: BASS-II
title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
tier_reason: Team list, Tier 1. PSI subarea: Spacecraft Fire Safety. Burning and suppression of solids.

summary_student.text: Astronauts burned plastic and fabric samples inside a small wind tunnel on the International Space Station to see how flames start, grow and go out without gravity. The results help engineers choose safer materials for spacecraft.

summary_professional.text: Ignition, flame growth, flame spread and extinction limits of solid fuels (rods, slabs, films and spherical sections) in low-velocity forced flow in microgravity. Airflow up to 40 cm/s and oxygen below 21% by nitrogen vitiation, with spread rates measured in opposed and concurrent flow. It bridges the normal-gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 method and material flammability in microgravity.

pillar.reason: It maps when solid materials ignite, spread flame and extinguish, which guides the selection of spacecraft materials.

environments.reason: The tests ran aboard the International Space Station in a glovebox wind tunnel.
Its stated goal is spacecraft fire safety on missions far from Earth.
